data.sentence: Aegis Cloud Security support, Elena Vasquez speaking — how can I help?
Hi Elena, it's Olivia Strand from Frostbyte AI, and Victor is on with me. We're stuck on the new attribute mapping screen in Identity.
Hi Olivia, hi Victor. Is this the redesigned mapping UI that went out last week?
Yes. We're trying to map our HR system's worker type field so contractors get a separate role, and the inline validation keeps rejecting it.
It says invalid attribute value, expected boolean. But the field is a string — employee, contractor, intern.
Okay, let me open your tenant. Which source attribute are you mapping from?
It's called workerType in our SCIM payload from the HR system.
I see it. The new UI is treating workerType as the built-in contractor flag, which is a true or false field, so it rejects the string values.
That's frustrating. We waited for this release specifically because the old mapping screen kept silently dropping this field.
We have about sixty contractors who still get full employee access, and our SOC 2 auditor flagged it last month.
Understood, that's a real access risk and I'll treat it that way.
There's a workaround. If you map workerType to a custom attribute instead of the built-in one, validation accepts strings.
Then you create an assignment rule — if the custom attribute equals contractor, assign the contractor role.
Let me try that now. Custom attribute... I'll call it hr_worker_type.
Okay, it saved. No validation error this time.
Now under assignment rules, add a condition on hr_worker_type equals contractor, and pick your contractor role.
Done. Do I need to force a sync, or will it pick it up on the next cycle?
I'd run a manual sync on a test user first, to be safe. Do you have a contractor account we can use?
Yes, I'll use mine, I set up a test contractor profile last week. Running it now.
It worked — the test account moved to the contractor role and lost access to the finance apps.
Good. That's the outcome we've been after since we left Okta.
But this is a workaround. We still don't have role inheritance, so our contractor role is a full copy of the employee role minus a few apps.
Every time we add an app, someone has to remember to update both roles. That's exactly how the audit finding happened.
That's fair. Hierarchical roles are on the Identity roadmap, and I'll add your case to the feature request so the team sees the audit impact.
Please do. Rachel said it might land in Q3, and a date would really help us with the auditor.
I'll ask the Identity product team for a target date and include it in my follow-up.
I'm also filing a bug on the validation behavior — the UI should let you choose a custom attribute instead of auto-matching the built-in flag.
Thanks. Can we roll this out to all sixty contractors today?
Yes, but I'd do it in two batches and check access reports after the first one, in case any contractor has an unusual app assignment.
Makes sense. I'll do the first thirty this afternoon.
Thanks Elena, that got us unblocked faster than I expected.
